header: The one-year window of every one-year chart (gold and silver, petrol and diesel, the dollar in rupees): it STARTS on the same date one year before today (today 13 November 2026: 13 November 2025) and ENDS today (or on the latest day the source has published, said so on the chart). People ask "what was the price on this day last year?", so I make the first point of the chart exactly that day. If the source has no figure for that exact day (a weekend, a holiday: gold, silver and the exchange rate are not published then) the first point holds the figure in force on that day, the last one published before it, and says so (`carried` is the date of the figure it really is). I invent nothing: the value is a real published one, and the chart says which day it was published. 29 February has no anniversary in most years: the window then starts on 28 February (Luxon's rule for "one year before").

symbols.name: yearAgo
symbols.sig: export function yearAgo(now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): string
doc: Returns the date one year before today, YYYY-MM-DD.

symbols.name: fromYearAgo
symbols.sig: export function fromYearAgo<T extends Dated>(points: T[], now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): Array<T & { carried?: string }>
doc: The points of a record from one year before today to its end. The first point is dated exactly one year back: the record's own point of that day, or a copy of the last point before it with that date and `carried` set to the day the figure really belongs to. A record that has no point on or before that day does not reach back a year: I return it as it is and leave it to the caller to decide what to say.

symbols.name: reachesYearAgo
symbols.sig: export function reachesYearAgo(points: Dated[], now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): boolean
doc: Tells whether the record reaches back to the anniversary (a point on or before it).

symbols.name: carryToToday
symbols.sig: export function carryToToday<T extends Dated>(points: T[], now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): { points: T[]; carriedFrom: string | null }
doc: For a price that stays as it is until the day it is changed (fuel): the record is carried forward to today with its last price, so the chart ends today. Returns the days added (0 when it already ends today). Use it only for such prices: I never carry a figure that is published each day (gold, the exchange rate) to a day it was not published.

behaviours: a year before 13 November 2026 is 13 November 2025
29 February has no anniversary in a common year: a year before 29 Feb 2028 is 28 Feb 2027, and a year before 1 March 2027 is 1 March 2026
the date is the Indian date: 1 am on 14 Nov in India is still 13 Nov in London, and the window follows India
a record with a point on the date: it begins on that very point (13 Nov 2025) and the earlier points are dropped
no point on the date (a weekend): the first point is dated exactly that day and holds the last figure before it, saying which day that was
the carried figure is a real published one (never invented): its value is that of the carried day
a record that does not reach back to the date is returned as it is
other fields of a point are kept (an estimate flag)
a price that stays until changed is carried on to today with its last value, saying from which day
a record that already ends today is not touched
